blocks.text: You can add an on-premises file servers to DSPM. DSPM scans the data assets for sensitive data and identifies any potential security posture risks.
Before adding an on-premises file server to DSPM, ensure the following prerequisites are met:

blocks.item: Integrate an on-premises scanner with DSPM to enable scanning of on-premises file servers. To learn more, see Adding or Deleting a Scanner Integration.
Create an on-premises data center and associate it with the configured on-premises scanner. To learn more, see Adding an On-Premises Data Center.
Configure the Network File System (NFS) client on the scanner host before you add NFS-based file servers. To learn more, see Configuring the NFS Client.
Add a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server for DSPM to map identities to file share entitlements. To learn more, see Adding an LDAP Server.

blocks.text: To add an on-premises file server:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Service Registration.
On the Service Registration page, select the On-Premises File Servers tab, and click Add File Server.
See image.
The Add On-Premises File Server drawer appears.
In the Add On-Premises File Server drawer:
File Server Information:
File Server Name: Enter a unique name for the file server.
Protocol: Select the communication protocol used to connect to the file server.
Version (available only if NFS protocol is selected): Select the NFS version to use.
File Server Type: Select the file server OS type.
NFS: Select Windows, Linux, or NetApp.
SMB: Select Windows, or NetApp.
Connection Attributes:
File Server IP / Hostname: Enter the IP address or hostname of the file server.
For an NFS protocol and NetApp file server type, enter the hostname only.
Domain Name: Enter the domain name associated with the file server.
Port: Select the port used for communication protocol.
Default Port: SMB uses 445 and NFS uses 2049.
Custom Port: Enter a valid port number based on your configuration requirements.
Authentication:
The authentication fields available depend on the Protocol and File Server Type selected.
Secret Provider Type: This field is autopopulated with the provider used to manage authentication secrets, typically set to Zscaler DSPM.
Authentication Type: Select the authentication method used to access file shares:
Kerberos: Uses Kerberos-based authentication to access file shares.
AUTH_SYS: Uses system-level User Identifier (UID) or Group Identifier (GID) credentials for authentication.
NTLMv2: Uses NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication to access file shares.
Username: Enter the username used to authenticate access to the file server.
Password: Enter the password associated with the username.
Group IDs: Enter one or more GIDs that have access to the file share, separated by commas.
The following table lists the availability of each field based on the selected protocol and file server type:

table: Available only when NetApp is selected as the file server type.
Available for NFS or SMB protocol with NetApp file server type.
Available for NFS protocol with NetApp file server type only.
Available for SMB protocol with NetApp file server type only.
Available for Windows or Linux file server types, or when Kerberos or NTLMv2 is selected for NetApp.
Available for Windows or Linux file server types, or when Kerberos or NTLMv2 is selected for NetApp.
Available only when AUTH_SYS is selected as the Authentication Type.

blocks.item: LDAP Server (available only when SMB is selected as the protocol):
Server (Optional): Select the registered LDAP server for the on-premises file server.
Data Center Association:
Data Center: Select the data center where the file server is located.
Location: This field is autopopulated based on the data center selection.
See image.
Click Save.
The Add On-Premises File Server confirmation window appears.
In the Add On-Premises File Server confirmation window, read the message, and then click Confirm and Save.
See image.

blocks.text: The on-premises file server is added and appears in the list on the On-Premises File Servers tab on the Service Registration page. DSPM starts to discover the file servers. If the discovery process fails, an error message is displayed in the Error column.
To configure the scan settings, see Configuring Scan Rule for On-Premises File Servers.
